content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% relative to historical mean.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves in history; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x the 30-day moving average of prior 7 days.
- Late-period forecasts (last 5–7 days) show persistent underestimation; adjust downward by 1–3% for each day beyond 20 days into forecast horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if history shows strong upward trend, forecast should gradually decline toward 30-day average; if downward, gradually rise toward it.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day spikes; smooth out forecast volatility by applying a 5-day moving average filter to raw forecast values before final output.
